title: Yaakov of Kefar Sikhnya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Yaakov of Kefar Sikhnya, one of that man’s disciples. Avodah Zarah 17a relates that Rabbi Eliezer told Rabbi Akiva how Yaakov once asked him: “Your Torah says, ‘You shall not bring a harlot’s hire,’ etc. May it be used to make a privy for the High Priest?” Rabbi Eliezer says that he answered nothing. Yaakov told him: “Thus I was taught: From filth they came; to filth they shall go.” The explanation pleased Rabbi Eliezer, and because of this he was punished. Kohelet Rabbah 1:8 also has the account. Perhaps he is Yaakov of Kefar Samma in Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14:4, who sought to heal Rabbi Elazar ben Dama in that man’s name, but Rabbi Yishmael prevented him. The end of Avodah Zarah 2:2 also has this.
Kohelet Rabbah 7:26 calls him Yaakov of Kefar Sessma.

notes.text: The first discussion concerns Rabbi Eliezer; the healing story’s Elazar ben Dama is explicitly spelled out in the checked Kohelet passage. Sessma is Hyman’s form, whereas the supplied and freshly checked Kohelet text has Sama. The identification between the village figures remains “perhaps.”

The consulted Avodah Zarah 17a names Yaakov of Kefar Sikhnya in Eliezer’s account; 27b names the would-be healer of Ben Dama. Kohelet Rabbah 7:26 separately has Elazar ben Dama and Yaakov of Kefar Sama. Hyman’s Samma/Sessma forms and perhaps identification remain, without automatic merging of the village figures or the two Eliezer/Elazar actors.
